question: Under the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025-2030, what daily protein target is recommended, in grams per kilogram of body weight?
answer: The 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day [1][6]. MedlinePlus gives the same range for both adults and children [8]. At least one group of authors has criticized the target as lacking a sufficient evidence base for a universal recommendation [1]. One J Nutr perspective argues that evidence from weight-loss studies is not broad enough to support a universal recommendation for all Americans across the lifespan [1]. Cleveland Clinic notes that extra protein doesn't necessarily bring extra benefits [6]. Personal protein needs are a question for your clinician or a registered dietitian.

studyNotes.focus: The question asks for the daily protein target in grams per kilogram of body weight set by the 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans.

keyPoints.text: The 2025-2030 Dietary Guidelines for Americans promote dietary protein intake of 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg/d.
Cleveland Clinic states the 2025-2030 guidelines recommend adults aim for 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day.
MedlinePlus states adult and child goals are 1.2 to 1.6 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day, citing the USDA/HHS 10th edition published January 2026.
The guidelines were released in early 2026 and recommend higher overall protein intake chiefly from animal sources.

conflicts.text: Source 1 says the protein recommendation lacks sufficient evidence as a universal target, while sources 6 and 8 present 1.2 to 1.6 g/kg/d simply as the official goal without that caveat.
